title: New insights into the domestication process of south American camelids at Telarmachay (Peru) from 9,000 to 4,500 years before present (BP)
version: Quaternary Science Reviews 376, 109819, DOI 10.1016/j.quascirev.2026.109819. Full article copy rendered online, publisher abstract checked.
lineage: Same rock shelter and legacy excavation corpus, shared Wheeler authorship. Adds separate shape, isotope, and mortality analyses, not a second excavation.

passages.note: Talus morphology changes in vicuña-like camelids in layer IV. The article interprets changed mobility as possible management intensification between modeled phase boundaries of 6.4–6.0 and 5.8–4.5 ka BP. The isotope results show no major change in diet or environment.
The reported bone morphology does not establish a shift to alpaca or llama phenotypes. The authors discuss protective herding as a possible alternative to captivity.
